content: The nerves that connect to the eye can be affected by a condition called optic neuropathy. If you experience changes in vision or symptoms such as pain, burning, tingling, numbness, or weakness in your arms, hands, legs, or feet while taking linezolid, stop the medication immediately and contact your healthcare provider. Seizures have been reported in some individuals taking linezolid. Seizures can present in various ways, some of which may not be easily recognizable. If you experience muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, or other uncontrolled movements, stiffening of the arms or legs, feelings of anxiety, nervousness, confusion, or dread, dizziness, lightheadedness, or loss of consciousness, stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea can occur due to an overgrowth of bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut, which may happen with many antibiotics, including linezolid. This condition can develop even up to two months after stopping the antibiotic. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in your stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever after starting or finishing the medication. Linezolid can cause low sodium levels in the blood (hyponatremia), which can be serious and potentially life-threatening. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels. Notify your provider if you experience nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory problems, weakness, fatigue, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, or balance issues. Linezolid may lead to a buildup of lactic acid in the blood, a condition known as lactic acidosis. Contact your healthcare provider if you experience rapid breathing, an abnormal or fast heartbeat, vomiting, extreme fatigue, or muscle weakness or cramps. Certain individuals should not take linezolid. This includes those allergic to linezolid, Zyvox, or any ingredients in the product. Linezolid should not be taken with certain medications, such as monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), tricyclic antidepressants, bupropion, triptans, buspirone, opioids, or medications for diabetes. Always inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Avoid consuming large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine while taking linezolid. These include aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects linezolid. Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat infections such as pneumonia, skin infections, and certain resistant bacterial infections. It works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis, preventing bacterial growth. However, it may not be effective for all infections, as some bacteria may be resistant to it. Linezolid is available as 600 mg oral tablets, 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension, and injectable forms. Store oral tablets and liquid at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) in a cool, dry place, protected from light. Do not shake the oral liquid; instead, turn the bottle upside down 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your provider, as the effects of linezolid on pregnancy and breastfeeding are not fully known. If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Complete the full course of treatment, even if symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. Contact your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions (e.g., breathing problems, swelling, hives), decreased blood cell production (myelosuppression), serotonin syndrome (e.g., confusion, agitation, fever, abnormal heartbeat, muscle stiffness, shivering, nausea, or diarrhea), and nerve damage (e.g., vision changes, pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness). Seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these serious side effects. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much linezolid, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222.
